However, there would be no need to 2 invest in permanent transportation infrastructure to service these emitter types; they would pull up to the berth at T-RICH to discharge their CO directly into the storage tanks using the existing piping systems 2 at T-RICH. 3.3.1 POWER PLANTS The largest target anthropogenic CO emission sources in the region are electricity generating power 2 plants. These CO sources are generally expected to adopt amine-based carbon capture systems due to 2 that technology’s high Technology Readiness Level (TRL). Prevalent exhaust emissions from industrial emitters in the region come from natural gas sources. According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), natural gas power plants account for about 75.2% of the total electricity generation in the Tampa Bay area. This is significantly higher than the national average of 42.3%. The high percentage of natural gas power plants in the Tampa Bay area is due to several factors, including the availability of natural gas resources, the environmental regulations in the area, the cost of electricity generation, increasingly prolonged heat and humidity, and the growing population in the Greater Tampa region and the state. The high percentage of natural gas power plants in the Tampa Bay 2 area has a few benefits. Natural gas is a cleaner-burning fuel than coal, and it produces fewer emissions of greenhouse gases and pollutants. Additionally, natural gas is a relatively inexpensive fuel, which helps to keep electricity prices low. The high percentage of natural gas power plants in the Tampa Bay area reflects the region's commitment to produce electricity from non-coal fuel sources. Development of the proposed hub would further the region’s sustainable energy and carbon reduction goals. However, it is important to be aware that natural gas power plants produce significant CO emissions. Thus, adopting 2 carbon capture systems on gas power plants will result in the production of clean power which will provide greater health benefits to state residents, assist in reducing CO emission levels in the state, and allow 2 power companies to meet future projected increases in power demand in Florida. The exhaust gas composition from a natural-gas power plant can vary depending on the efficiency of the power plant and the specific type of natural gas used.
